questionText:
A system has a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) that has a reach of 1 MB. TLB reach is defined as the total amount of physical memory that can be accessed through the TLB entries. The paging system uses pages of size 4 KB. The virtual address space is 64 GB and physical address space is 1 GB. If each TLB entry stores a 4-bit process id, page number, frame number, and a 2-bit control field, then the size of the TLB (in bytes) is ____________. (answer in integer)

Note: 1K=$2^{10}$, 1M=$2^{20}$, 1G=$2^{30}$
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the number of entries in the TLB.
• $\text{TLB Reach} = 1\text{ MB} = 2^{20}\text{ bytes}$
• $\text{Page Size} = 4\text{ KB} = 2^{12}\text{ bytes}$
• $\text{Number of TLB Entries} = \frac{\text{TLB Reach}}{\text{Page Size}} = \frac{2^{20}}{2^{12}} = 2^8 = 256\text{ entries}$

Step 2: Calculate bits required for Page Number and Frame Number.
• $\text{Virtual Address Space} = 64\text{ GB} = 2^{36}\text{ bytes} \Rightarrow 36\text{-bit Virtual Address}$
• $\text{Page Offset} = \log_2(4\text{ KB}) = 12\text{ bits}$
• $\text{Page Number Bits} = 36 - 12 = 24\text{ bits}$

• $\text{Physical Address Space} = 1\text{ GB} = 2^{30}\text{ bytes} \Rightarrow 30\text{-bit Physical Address}$
• $\text{Frame Offset} = \log_2(4\text{ KB}) = 12\text{ bits}$
• $\text{Frame Number Bits} = 30 - 12 = 18\text{ bits}$

Step 3: Calculate the size of a single TLB entry.
• $\text{Size of 1 TLB Entry} = \text{Process ID} + \text{Page Number} + \text{Frame Number} + \text{Control Field}$
• $\text{Size of 1 TLB Entry} = 4\text{ bits} + 24\text{ bits} + 18\text{ bits} + 2\text{ bits} = 48\text{ bits} = 6\text{ bytes}$

Step 4: Calculate the total TLB size in bytes.
• $\text{Total TLB Size} = 256\text{ entries} \times 6\text{ bytes/entry} = 1536\text{ bytes}$
